spec.name: Trend v3
spec.notes: Classic trend signal on trailing returns. Weekly rebalance.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.5, annual return 9%, maximum drawdown 14%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.47 to 1.41 (change -0.06).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.47 to 1.47. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.46 (as submitted, 8 bps: 1.47); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is -0.28 against 1.47 as submitted; the strategy never saw 139 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is -0.26 against 1.47 in research, a gap of +1.74.
The best year gives 31% of total P&L (year 1) and calm regimes give 152%; Sharpe is 3.19 in calm and -2.66 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 5 distinct specs; the best of 5 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.25, so the claimed 1.50 becomes 1.25 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.53 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.03, 95th percentile 0.60).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.47 to as low as 1.10 (as low as 1.16 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (20 days) give 33% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 43% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

exhibits.summary: The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (survivorship_test EX-4, holdout_test EX-5).
